name: Zaccur
overview: Zaccur was a male member of the tribe of Simeon, identified specifically as the son of Hammuel. He is noted in Scripture as a Simeonite, emphasizing his tribal affiliation within Israel. Beyond his lineage, there are no additional personal details recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Zaccur means "remembering," reflecting a proper name recorded in the Old Testament. This name was not given directly by God but is noted in 1 Chronicles 4:26, indicating its Hebrew origin and significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Zaccur as the son of Hammuel. It is also inferred that Shimei was his father, though this is not directly stated. No other family relationships are recorded for Zaccur beyond these connections.
scriptureSignificance: Zaccur's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Simeon, as documented in the genealogies of 1 Chronicles. His mention helps preserve the record of Simeonite descendants, which is important for understanding the tribal divisions and heritage of Israel. While not a prominent figure in biblical narratives, his inclusion underscores the faithfulness of God in maintaining His covenant people through their lineage.
